title: TESS eclipse times from 2018 to 2025 do not agree with nine published circumbinary-companion timing models of seven post-common-envelope binaries
abstract: We measured 5,489 primary-eclipse times of 11 post-common-envelope binaries in 44 TESS sectors with one symmetric-template method. Sector timing uncertainties are 0.06 to 2.1 s (V471 Tau: 4 to 10 s). Single-eclipse scatter agrees with the formal errors for the sdB systems, 20-s and 120-s times agree within 1.8 sigma, FFI times agree after a target-specific barycentric correction (the TESScut correction differs by up to 36 s), and TESS agrees with contemporaneous ground times to -4.6 to +1.6 s. We then tested nine published light-travel-time (circumbinary planet or brown dwarf) models of HW Vir, HS0705+6700, DE CVn, V471 Tau, NY Vir, NSVS 07826147 and Kepler-451. After each model's data end, TESS times differ from the predictions by 7 to 189 s, many times the TESS errors. The two 2026 Kepler-451 models, fitted to these TESS data, leave 3.0 to 3.3 s RMS after a free linear term (chi-square 46 and 55 for 6 dof). RR Cae is 30 s from the 2025 quadratic ephemeris of Pulley et al. four to six months after their data end, and their printed QS Vir quadratic coefficient probably has a sign error. TESS alone detects O-C curvature in six of seven multi-sector systems, but not in HS0705+6700. Limitations: one to eight sectors per system, rounded or incomplete published parameters, and a possible few-second TESS-ground clock offset. We report no new planet.
